question.text: Find all the real solutions to the equation $5b^3+12b^2+20b+48=0.$
question.explanation:
We proceed to factor the left-hand side by grouping:

\begin{align} 5b^3+12b^2+20b+48 &= \\ (5b^3+12b^2) + (20b+48) &= \\ b^2(5b+12) +4(5b+12) &= \\ (5b+12) \cdot b^2 + (5b+12) \cdot 4 &= \\ (5b+12)(b^2+4)& . \end{align}

Then, we solve $(5b+12)(b^2+4) = 0$ by setting each factor equal to $0.$

  • Setting the factor $(5b+12)$ equal to $0,$ we get \begin{align*} 5b+12&= 0\\[5pt] 5b &= -12\\[5pt] b&=-\dfrac{12}{5}. \end{align*}

  • Setting the factor $(b^2+4)$ equal to $0,$ we get \begin{align} b^2+4 &= 0 \\ b^2 &= -4. \end{align} Since a squared real number cannot be negative, the equation $b^2+4=0$ has no real solutions.

Therefore, $b=-\dfrac{12}{5}$ is the only real solution.

question.text: Find all of the real solutions to the equation $8z^3-z^2+40z-5=0.$
question.explanation:
We proceed to factor the left-hand side by grouping:

\begin{align} 8z^3-z^2+40z-5 &= \\ (8z^3-z^2) + (40z-5) &= \\ z^2(8z-1) +5(8z-1) &= \\ (8z-1) \cdot z^2 + (8z-1) \cdot 5 &= \\ (8z-1)(z^2+5)& . \end{align}

Then, we solve $(8z-1)(z^2+5) = 0$ by setting each factor equal to $0.$

  • Setting the factor $(8z-1)$ equal to $0,$ we get \begin{align*} 8z-1 &= 0\\ 8z &= 1\\ z & = \dfrac {1}{8}. \end{align*}

  • Setting the factor $(z^2+5)$ equal to $0,$ we get \begin{align} z^2+5 &= 0 \\ z^2 &= -5. \end{align} Since a squared real number cannot be negative, the equation $z^2+5=0$ has no real solutions.

Therefore, $z= \dfrac {1}{8}$ is the only real solution.

example.title: Solving Cubic Equations With Leading Coefficients by Grouping

question.explanation:
First, we multiply the equation by $-1$ to make the coefficient of the cubic term positive. This gives

\[ y^3-3y^2-2y+6= 0. \]

We then proceed to factor the left-hand side by grouping:

\begin{align*} y^3-3y^2-2y+6 & = \\ (y^3-3y^2)+(-2y+6) & = \\ y^2(y-3) - 2(y-3)& = \\ (y^2-2)(y-3)&\\ \end{align*}

Then, we solve $(y^2-2)(y-3)=0$ by setting each factor equal to $0.$

  • Setting the factor $(y^2-2)$ equal to $0,$ we get $y = \pm \sqrt 2.$

  • Setting the factor $(y - 3)$ equal to $0,$ we get $y=3.$

Therefore, the solutions are $y= 3, \, \pm \sqrt 2.$
